segments.text: The whole sky has turned red.
But sunlight itself is the same color day or night.
It's actually white light, made of every color mixed together.
Tiny air molecules scatter blue light more than any other color.
That scattered blue light is what makes the daytime sky blue.
At sunset the sun sits low, so light travels a much longer path through the air.
Along that long stretch, the blue light scatters off in other directions
and only the red and orange light makes it all the way to your eyes.
That's why sunsets glow red and orange.
